The plaint case is that the original owners of the land appertaining to CS khatian No. 62 were Safarunessa, Ayeb Ali, Amsory Bibi and Jobirar Nessa and the CS record was correctly prepared in their names. They were the owners of the suit land measuring 5.26 acres of CS plot No. 1356 and 1357 appertaining to CS khatian No. 62. After the death of Safarunnesa, Ayeb Ali was the owner and was in possession of 1.97½ acre, of land Amsory Bibi and Jobirar Nessa were the owners in possession of 1.64½ acres and 1.64 acres of land respectively out of 5.26 acres of total land. 

 8. Defendant Nos. 14, 16, 25, 26, 27 and 31-38 contested the suit by filing written statement stating inter alia, that Mohor Ali was the original owner of 5.26 acre land of CS plot No. 1356, appertaining to CS Khatian No. 62, measuring 5.26 acres of land. 

 12. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the learned Court decided issue Nos. 1 and 3 in favour of the plaintiff-appellants but ultimately dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs had no title in the suit land and, as such, the suit for partition was dismissed. He submits that on the basis of deposition of DW 2 Md Sirajul Haque, the learned trial Court held that the Mutant suit for partition was bad for defect of parties. But on that ground a suit for partition cannot be dismissed. Asa matter of fact, due to misreading and non-reading of the plaint and the material evidence, the learned trial Court came to a vivid wrong finding that Shajahan, Abdur Rahman and Jahanara Begum were not made parties in the suit. While Shajahan was made defendant No. 41 and Jahanara Begum was made defendant No. 38 and Abdur Rahman was made defendant No. 10 in the plaint and also their names appear in the decree. Regarding the heirs of Hashem, DW 2 was made defendant No. 15, who stated in his cross-examination that the share of the suit property has been mutated in his name as he gave some land to his sisters from elsewhere and, as such, the sister of defendant No. 15. Sirajul Hoque is not a necessary party in the instant suit. Therefore the learned trial Court is absolutely wrong in holding that the suit is bad for defect of parties and, as such, the judgment is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that defendant Nos. 42, 39, 15 and 24, 40 and 41 admitted in their cross-examination that the suit land originally belonged to Ayeb Ali, Amsory Bibi, Jobirarrnessa and Sofurunessa according to CS Khatian, PW 1 stated in his cross-examination that Mohor Ali was not the owner of any suit property mentioned in the plaint and, as such, the question of selling the suit land to some-body does not arise at all. He further submits that defendant No. 14, 16, 25, 26, 27, 31-38 stated in their written statement that the suit property measuring 5.26 originally belonged to Mohor Ali and this Mohar Ali sold 2.45 acres of land to one Yasin by a registered deed No. 5577 dated 28-4-1928 but they did not produce the said original deed before the learned trial Court. The plaintiffs after taking certified copy of deed No. 5577 dated 28-4-28 found that the vendor and vendee of the deed of sale are altogether different persons having no connection with the suit property and, as such, the learned trial Court failed to consider the same and fell in error. He lastly submits that the defendants totally failed to prove their case as they could not establish any right and title of Yasin over the suit property by adducing any oral or documentary evidence and, as such, all the subsequent transactions are false and fraudulent. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate refers to a decision in the case of Firoja Mazib vs JB Corporation reported in 39 DLR (AD) 78 on the point of admissibly of oral evidence to contradict the terms of the contents of a document under section 92 of Evidence Act, the decision was in negative.
